title: What is a File?
drDigitalIntro:
Everything you keep on a computer is stored as a file.
• A photo is a file. A typed letter is a file. A song is a file.
• Each file has a name and holds one piece of your stuff.
• When you open a file, a window appears with the file's name in the title bar.
• The X in the corner closes the window. It does not delete the file.
• Open a couple below and see what is in them.

playgroundTask.goal: Open two files to see what a file is

steps.say: Double-click GroceryList.txt to open it. A window will pop up — read what's inside, then click Got it — Close.
That file held a list of words. Files can hold pictures too — double-click VacationPhoto.png to open it.

drDigitalSuccess: You opened two files. One held words, one held a picture. Closing the window does not delete anything; the file stays where it was.
drDigitalHint: Double-click means two quick clicks on the same file. Look for the file with a yellow glow. After it opens, read the contents and then click Got it — Close.
